params.name: video_query
params.why: The search text supplied by the task; differs across every run.

params.name: initial_watch_time
params.why: Duration to watch before fast-forwarding; differs across every run's wait step.

params.name: final_watch_time
params.why: Duration to watch after fast-forwarding; differs across every run's final wait step.

params.name: fast_forward_time
params.why: Total seconds to fast-forward, as stated by the task; the per-press seek amount (10s) recorded on the media lines anchors the derived press-count parameter.

params.name: fast_forward_presses
params.why: The site seeks 10s per 'l' press (seen on every press's media line). Press count = fast_forward_time / 10: 30/10=3 (r1), 20/10=2 (r2), 40/10=4 (r5), matching the recorded press counts exactly.

main.why: Start at youtube.com, the task's declared start URL.
Fill the search box with the video query; every run used a different query text (parameterized).
Submit the search by clicking the search button (r1, r2). r5 achieved the equivalent by pressing Enter (r5.s2.0) instead; kept the click form from the majority behavior.
Task says play the FIRST video that pops up — a position, not a specific title. Every run clicked index 0 of the structural results ladder even though the clicked video's own name differed per query.

Watch the video for the declared initial period before fast-forwarding. r5's true match is r5.s7.0 (18s, on the real video after the ad was skipped), not the auto-aligned r5.s5.0 which was an ad-buffering wait.

body.why: Press 'l' on the video element to seek forward; every run's media line shows exactly +10s per press.

main.why: Fast-forward gesture: repeated 'l' presses (10s each) until reaching fast_forward_time total (3 presses=30s in r1, 2=20s in r2, 4=40s in r5).
Final watch period after fast-forwarding completes, per task.

interrupts.why: Task: 'If an ad is shown skip the ad.' The Skip button was clicked only in the runs that encountered an ad (r1, r5); r2's video had no ad, so this cannot be a main-path edge.
Task: 'If at any point any pop-ups happen dismiss them.' The 'No thanks' promo was dismissed in r1 and r5 but never appeared in r2.

accept.why: The workflow must end on the video's watch page, not still on the search results.
The player must still be actively playing content through the final watch period, proving the task did not silently stall or get blocked by an undismissed overlay.

notes: Runs 3 and 4 were NOT achieved (run 3 got stuck repeating a press action 6 times on the same element; run 4's stop message is truncated/ambiguous about final success) and were excluded from kept_runs. No per-step transcript was provided for runs 3/4 in this round, so no ExcludedRun evidence step could be honestly cited — exclusion is based solely on the recorded 'achieved' status.

Search submission was flaky in two of three runs: r1 and r5 each needed a second click on the search button (r1.s3.0, r5.s3.0) because a suggestions dropdown still covered results after the first submit action; r2 needed only one click. Treated the second clicks as duplicate/UI-retry noise and left them off the main path.

r5 submitted the search via the Enter key (r5.s2.0) rather than clicking the search button. Kept the click-based submit edge from the spine (matching r1 and r2's button click) as the main-path action and noted the Enter-key alternative here instead of forcing it into corroborated_by (different action type).

r5.s5.0 (wait 5s) was actually a wait for the ad/skip button to render, not the declared initial_watch_time value — the code aligner mismatched it to that column. The genuine initial_watch_time wait for r5 is r5.s7.0 (18s, taken on the real video right after the ad was skipped), which was used for both the main-path corroboration and the parameter witness.

The first-result click was modeled positionally (structural rung, nth=0) rather than by name, since the clicked video's title differs completely across runs (it follows each run's distinct query) — the task means 'the first video that pops up', a position not an identity.

Ad-skip and 'No thanks' popup-dismiss clicks were modeled as interrupts rather than main-path edges because run2 encountered neither, and the task text itself frames both as conditional ('if an ad is shown...', 'if any pop-ups happen...').

Fast-forward was modeled as a derived-count repeat: every kept run pressed the seek key ('l') in discrete +10s increments per the recorded media deltas, with press counts (3/2/4) exactly matching fast_forward_time/10 for 30s/20s/40s respectively — supporting a clean derived parameter rather than a fixed constant.
